subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where sender canonicalizes to destination_caller_id, should OpenClaw only repair when a canonical peer is recoverable, or should it also drop fail-closed before access control when no peer can be recovered?
rationale: That choice controls whether ambiguous local-sender payloads can reach authorization, pairing, routing, and reply delivery, so it is an identity-boundary policy decision beyond the mechanical normalization fix.

options.title: Repair Confident Canonical Peers
options.body: Require normalizeIMessageHandle comparisons, repair only when a distinct canonical peer is found, and require live after-fix proof before merge.

options.title: Repair Then Drop Ambiguous Payloads
options.body: Repair confident peers and drop ambiguous local-sender DMs before access control when the peer cannot be recovered safely.

options.title: Pause For Separate Root Cause
options.body: If the author’s remaining failure is not this race, pause this branch and track the narrower iMessage identity issue separately.

recommendation.title: Repair Confident Canonical Peers
recommendation.body: Require normalizeIMessageHandle comparisons, repair only when a distinct canonical peer is found, and require live after-fix proof before merge.
